question: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted during the regime of which viceroy of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Lytton.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Vernacular Press Act 1878:**

__
 
• ​__British India passed the Vernacular Press Act (1878) to **restrict press freedom and discourage criticism of British policy,** notably the opposition that had risen since the commencement of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–80).
 
• **The Act was submitted by Lytton, the Viceroy of India at the time, and on March 14, 1878, **the Viceroy's Council unanimously approved it. In order to "better control" the vernacular press and effectively penalize and prohibit "seditious literature" in "publications in oriental languages," the Vernacular Press Act (VPA) was passed.
 
• As a result, the British had nothing but hatred for the (non-English speaking) Indian press.
 
• It was also known as the Gagging Act.
 
• It was an act for the better control of publication in oriental languages.
 
• It was primarily targeted against Amrit Bazar Patrika.
 
• The act was repealed by Lord Ripon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Dalhousie was the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. He was known for his policies of annexation and modernization, including the Doctrine of Lapse and the construction of railways and telegraph lines.
 
• Lord Hastings was the Governor-General of India from 1813 to 1823. He was known for his military campaigns, including the Anglo-Nepalese War and the First Anglo-Burmese War.
 
• Lord Ripon was the Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884. He was known for his liberal policies, including the repeal of the Vernacular Press Act and the introduction of local self-government.
